source: "Claude Code Resource Bible" poster shared in the SATNA_PROJECT community on Reddit

tools.name: Beginner → Advanced Guide
tools.summary: A three-part newsletter issue that takes non-developers from installing Claude Code and setting up project context, through running workflows with parallel agents, to using it to run a business.

tools.name: Official Docs
tools.summary: Anthropic's documentation for Claude Code: install, quickstart, CLAUDE.md memory, skills, hooks, MCP, subagents, scheduled tasks, and every surface (terminal, IDE, desktop, web).

tools.name: Partner Network
tools.summary: Anthropic's March 2026 announcement of the Claude Partner Network, a program for firms that help enterprises adopt Claude, backed by $100M for training, support, and joint marketing.
tools.note: Aimed at consultancies and integrators, not individual users.

tools.name: Certification
tools.summary: Access request for the Claude Certified Architect – Foundations exam. It lives in the Partner Network's learning portal.

tools.name: MCP Servers Repo
tools.summary: The MCP steering group's reference servers, meant to demonstrate the protocol and SDKs.
tools.note: These are reference examples, not production servers. For a full catalog, the repo points to the MCP Registry at registry.modelcontextprotocol.io.

tools.name: Everything Claude Code
tools.summary: Home page for ECC, an open-source toolkit of skills, hooks, planning tools, shared memory, and a security scanner (AgentShield) for Claude Code and Codex, with an optional paid GitHub App.
tools.note: Same project as #6. It's a toolkit you install, not a directory of other tools.

tools.name: Mega Resource Repo
tools.summary: The GitHub repo behind ECC (#5): skills, hooks, and agent tooling in 16 languages.
tools.note: The README asks you to install only from github.com/affaan-m/ECC, the npm packages ecc-universal and ecc-agentshield, or ecc.tools.

tools.name: Awesome MCP Servers
tools.summary: A long, community-curated list of MCP servers sorted by category, plus clients, tutorials, and frameworks.

tools.name: Awesome Claude Skills
tools.summary: A curated list of Claude Skills. The cheat sheet misspelled the account name.

tools.name: Skill Codex
tools.summary: A Claude Code plugin that lets Claude hand work to OpenAI's Codex CLI (codex exec) for analysis, refactoring, and edits.
tools.note: Needs the Codex CLI installed and signed in.

tools.name: Visual Skills Browser
tools.summary: An install page for cmux skills: copy one prompt, paste it into Claude Code, and it writes a skill for managing several agents from one terminal.

tools.name: 50+ Best MCP Addons
tools.summary: A categorized directory of 50+ MCP servers and Claude Code extensions: IDE integrations, usage monitors, orchestrators, and more.

tools.name: MCP Server Guide
tools.summary: AgentCat's (formerly MCPcat) guide to MCP servers for Claude Code, grouped by use with install commands for each.

tools.name: Playwright
tools.summary: Microsoft's official Playwright MCP server. Lets Claude drive a browser through accessibility snapshots instead of screenshots.
tools.note: It's Microsoft's, not Anthropic's. The README suggests coding agents try Playwright CLI + skills, which uses fewer tokens.

tools.name: Firecrawl
tools.summary: Firecrawl's official MCP server: web search, scraping any URL into clean data, and an index of GitHub issues, PRs, and docs.

tools.name: Supabase
tools.summary: Connects Claude to your Supabase projects to manage tables, fetch config, and query data.
tools.note: Supabase asks you to read its MCP security best practices before connecting.

tools.name: PostgreSQL
tools.summary: Postgres MCP Pro: index tuning, explain plans, database health checks, and safe SQL execution.
tools.note: The cheat sheet's repo doesn't exist. This is a well-known working replacement, not necessarily what the cheat sheet meant.

tools.name: GitHub
tools.summary: GitHub's official MCP server: browse code, manage issues and PRs, and monitor Actions runs.

tools.name: Sentry
tools.summary: Sentry's official remote MCP server, tuned for debugging with coding agents. Same repo holds the Sentry CLI.

tools.name: Dokploy
tools.summary: Exposes the whole Dokploy deployment API (500+ tools) to MCP clients. Requires your own Dokploy server.

tools.name: Slack
tools.summary: A popular community Slack MCP server: channels, DMs, and history search over stdio, SSE, or HTTP.
tools.note: Community-built, not from Slack. It advertises a no-permissions 'stealth mode'; check with your workspace admin before using it on a work Slack.

tools.name: Notion
tools.summary: Notion's self-hosted MCP server.
tools.note: Notion says this repo is no longer maintained and recommends its hosted Remote Notion MCP (developers.notion.com/docs/mcp) instead.

tools.name: Figma
tools.summary: Framelink MCP for Figma: paste a Figma link and the agent reads real design data to build the UI.
tools.note: Community-built replacement for the dead link.

tools.name: Linear
tools.summary: A community Linear MCP server for reading and updating issues.
tools.note: Its author deprecated it in favor of Linear's official remote MCP server (mcp.linear.app). Use that.

tools.name: 10 CLI Tools for AI Coding
tools.summary: Terminal tools that pair well with coding agents: LazyGit, Glow, LLM Fit, Models CLI, Taproom, Ranger, Zoxide, Btop, Chafa, CSV Lens, plus eza.

tools.name: Best MCP Servers for Devs
tools.summary: An intro to MCP plus a ranked list of ten developer MCP servers and eight honorable mentions.
tools.note: Written by Firecrawl, which ranks its own server first.

tools.name: MCP Config Guide
tools.summary: Builder.io's guide to adding MCP servers to Claude Code: config scopes, useful servers, Tool Search for saving context, and fixing connection problems.

tools.name: Agentmaxxing
tools.summary: A guide to running Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI in parallel: terminal setups, git worktrees, workflow, and practical limits.
tools.note: The cheat sheet's link wouldn't load and couldn't be found. This March 2026 article by the same name is the closest match.

tools.name: Superpowers
tools.summary: A full software-development method for coding agents, built from composable skills: brainstorm, plan, test-first build, and review.
tools.note: Wrong account name and wrong description on the cheat sheet. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and others.

tools.name: Taste Skill
tools.summary: Portable agent skills that push AI-built interfaces past generic defaults with stronger layout and design judgment.

tools.name: Chrome CDP
tools.summary: Lets your agent see and act in the Chrome you already have open, including tabs where you're signed in.
tools.note: Because it uses your real logins, the agent can reach your email and accounts. Use it deliberately.

tools.name: Delivery Lifecycle
tools.summary: Plugin skills for Claude Code and Codex covering idea vetting, fixes, architecture review, and deploys, each with a defined check and evidence report.

tools.name: Codex Settings
tools.summary: A ready-made setup for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, and Cursor: skills, commands, hooks, subagents, and MCP servers.

tools.name: CLUI
tools.summary: A floating macOS overlay for Claude Code with multi-tab sessions, a permission approval panel, voice input, and a skills marketplace.

tools.name: Loop
tools.summary: A desktop app for recording screen videos, transcribing as you talk, and cutting dead air from the transcript into a finished MP4.
tools.note: Not a task runner. For recurring prompts, Claude Code has a built-in /loop command and scheduled tasks (see #1).

tools.name: Clawd Cursor
tools.summary: A desktop-control engine for AI agents: maps the screen into UI elements, acts on them, verifies each action, and routes everything through one safety checkpoint.
tools.note: Unrelated to the Cursor editor.

tools.name: cmux
tools.summary: A free, open-source native macOS terminal built on Ghostty, with vertical tabs and alerts when an agent needs you.

tools.name: gmux
tools.summary: A Ghostty + tmux setup for running Claude Code, Codex, and opencode side by side, configured with dotfiles instead of a new app.

tools.name: claude-squad
tools.summary: A terminal app that runs several agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Aider) at once, each in its own git workspace, with review before you apply changes.

tools.name: dmux
tools.summary: Runs parallel coding agents in tmux panes, each on its own git worktree, then merges the branches back.

tools.name: mux
tools.summary: Coder's coding-agent multiplexer: isolated workspaces (local, worktree, or SSH) with one view of how each has diverged.
tools.note: Renamed to Xum after a trademark concern.

tools.name: ClawTeam
tools.summary: Give one goal and agents form a team: spawn helpers, delegate, and deliver. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other CLI agents.

tools.name: CLI-Anything
tools.summary: Generates command-line interfaces for existing software so agents can operate it, with a community hub of ready-made CLIs.

tools.name: Collaborator AI
tools.summary: A desktop app that lays out terminals, context files, and running code on one infinite canvas for working with agents.
tools.note: Early-stage and changing quickly.

tools.name: Autoresearch
tools.summary: Turns Claude Code, OpenCode, or Codex into an improvement loop: set a goal and a metric, and the agent iterates until it gets there. Based on Karpathy's autoresearch.

tools.name: ACE Platform
tools.summary: Open-source platform that turns one-off prompts into playbooks that improve after each task, connected to Claude Code and Codex over MCP.

tools.name: Hermes Agent
tools.summary: Nous Research's self-improving agent: it writes skills from experience, searches its own past conversations, and runs on a VPS or serverless.

tools.name: CopilotKit
tools.summary: Toolkit for putting agents inside your own app: generative UI, shared state, and human-in-the-loop for React, Angular, Vue, Slack, and Teams.

tools.name: n8n-as-code
tools.summary: Build, edit, deploy, and debug n8n workflows from VS Code or Cursor with an agent that sees your live n8n setup.

tools.name: Office Agents
tools.summary: Microsoft Office add-ins with an AI chat panel that can read and write your Word and Excel files, using your own API key.

tools.name: Cloak Browser
tools.summary: A modified Chromium built to pass bot detection, usable as a drop-in Playwright or Puppeteer replacement.
tools.note: Its purpose is getting past anti-bot checks. Check a site's terms before pointing it there.

tools.name: OpenLogs
tools.summary: Collects raw events from your apps, APIs, workers, and infrastructure so coding agents can read real logs when diagnosing failures.

tools.name: Vercel Chat SDK
tools.summary: Vercel's open-source toolkit for running one bot codebase across many chat platforms (March 2026 announcement).

tools.name: Self-Hosted Infra
tools.summary: How to run your own Happy relay server, the piece that carries encrypted sessions between your computer and the Happy mobile app for Claude Code.
tools.note: These docs cover the original Happy CLI, now in maintenance mode; the newer Happy desktop app gets the new features.
